content_voiceover: This is a dense but extremely high-yield summary slide for ALL risk stratification, worth memorizing in detail. Start with the NCI clinical criteria, standard risk means age one to under ten years, white count under fifty thousand, and no extramedullary involvement, anything outside that, younger than one, older than ten, higher white count, or extramedullary disease, bumps a patient to high risk. Next, the cancer genome panel groups cytogenetics into three tiers. Low risk includes hyperdiploidy over fifty chromosomes, the ETV6-RUNX1 fusion, trisomies four and ten, and for T-ALL, NOTCH1 or FBXW7 mutations. Intermediate risk includes ZNF384 fusions, DUX4 and ERG deregulated subtypes, the TCF3-PBX1 fusion, and for T-ALL, PTEN inactivation or MLL rearrangement. High risk includes the Philadelphia chromosome and Ph-like disease with BCR-ABL1 fusion, KMT2A rearrangements, intrachromosomal amplification of chromosome twenty one, hypodiploidy under forty four chromosomes, IKZF1 and TP53 mutations, MEF2D fusions, and for T-ALL, early T-cell precursor phenotype. The host genome panel covers pharmacogenomics you'll be tested on directly, TPMT and NUDT15 variants predict thiopurine-induced myelosuppression, CEP72 variants predict vincristine peripheral neuropathy, BMP7 and PROX1 antisense RNA variants are linked to glucocorticoid-induced osteonecrosis, and SLCO1B1, DHFR, and miR-1206 variants predict methotrexate-induced mucositis. Finally, minimal residual disease status drives treatment intensity, negative MRD supports treatment reduction in favorable genotypes, while positive MRD prompts intensified chemotherapy or consideration of cellular therapy.
keypoints: NCI risk: age 1-10 plus WBC under 50k, no extramedullary disease, equals standard risk
Favorable: hyperdiploidy over 50, ETV6-RUNX1; Unfavorable: Ph/Ph-like, KMT2A, hypodiploid under 44, IKZF1, TP53
MRD-negative favors de-escalation; MRD-positive favors intensification or cellular therapy
keypoint_voiceover: For the exam, anchor on four buckets: the NCI standard versus high-risk clinical criteria, the three-tier cytogenetic risk groups, the host pharmacogenomic gene-drug-toxicity pairs, and how MRD status directly changes treatment intensity.
